own_solution.law: Energy balance: P t = m c dT, t = m c dT / P
assumptions: all heater output goes into the water, no losses (authors assume this; the item text does not state it)

defect_reasons.missing_assumption: The authors' own first assumption ('all of the heater power goes into the water and no heat is lost') is needed for the certified answer but is not stated in the item, and any heat loss gives a materially longer time.

counterexamples: With 80% of the 1500 W reaching the water, t = 334880/1200 = 279.1 s, not 223.25 s.
notes: Numerical claims all check: base 2*4186*40/1500 = 223.253 s; jug mixed in at 0.5/1/2 kg gives 2.5/3/4 kg and 279.067/334.88/446.507 s. Minimal pairs T4D81<->T581F and T808E<->TD5BB state the same 1 kg at the same starting temperature and differ only in attachment. Initial-temperature sentences: in pass 1 I labelled them K (matters only if the rise would cross boiling); the authors label them C via T_final - T_initial cancelling. Both readings are defensible; for listed values 283-303 K the final temperature stays at or below 343 K, so no phase change and the C claim holds; I accept C and do not flag it. The only defect remains the unstated no-heat-loss/full-power-transfer condition, which the authors list as an assumption but the problem text omits ('rated at 1500 W' is not the same as 1500 W delivered to the water). I keep it high under rule 1's strict standard, with moderate confidence because it is commonly left implicit in textbook problems.
